#4246. A common blood pressure drug has a surprising effect on calorie-burning brown fat

A widely used blood pressure medication may have an unexpected benefit beyond its ability to control hypertension. Scientists have found that losartan can activate brown fat, a specialized type of body fat that burns energy, and improve metabolic activity in mice. The discovery suggests that an existing medication could potentially be repurposed to stimulate brown fat and support metabolic health.

Losartan belongs to a class of medications called angiotensin receptor blockers (ARB), which have an established safety profile. In a new study published in Nature, researchers found that the drug increased brown fat activity through a biological mechanism separate from its blood pressure effects. This raises the possibility of developing treatments that activate brown fat without lowering blood pressure.

The findings also revealed a surprising connection between brown fat and mental health. After examining data from more than 100,000 patients, researchers discovered that people with detectable brown fat had lower rates of several medical conditions, including anxiety and depression. This is the first time the research team has reported associations between brown fat and psychiatric health, adding to earlier evidence linking the tissue to better cardiovascular and metabolic health.

The research was led by Paul Cohen at Rockefeller University's Laboratory of Molecular Metabolism, working with Heiko Schöder and Daniel Lafontaine from Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center (MSKCC). It expands on research published in 2021, when Cohen's team analyzed approximately 50,000 patients and found that those with more brown fat had substantially lower odds of developing cardiometabolic conditions such as coronary artery disease and type II diabetes.

"We only looked for a few diagnostic codes in that study, mainly focusing on cardiovascular disease since that's what this tissue has historically been associated with," says Cohen. "The scope of this new analysis is far more expansive. We doubled our number of patients and considered more than 500 codes, which allowed us to unearth many new insights."

AI Analysis Reveals New Benefits of Brown Fat

To investigate brown fat's relationship with human health, the researchers examined PET/CT scans from more than 100,000 patients who had undergone imaging as part of their cancer monitoring. They focused on scans showing brown adipose tissue, which can be found in six regions of the body, including the neck, armpits, and areas around organs such as the heart and kidneys.

The team used an approach known as reverse translation, which begins with observations in patients and then investigates the biological processes responsible for them. Cohen's laboratory has previously used this strategy to uncover important details about brown fat and its effects on health.

Nicolás Gómez-Banoy, the study's first author and an endocrinologist and instructor in clinical investigation in Cohen's laboratory, used a machine learning system developed by researchers at MSKCC to measure brown fat activity. The technology allowed him to assess both the total activity in each patient and the activity within each of the six anatomical regions.

The analysis showed that brown fat's location could be just as important as its presence. Activity in particular regions appeared to have stronger associations with certain health conditions, suggesting that brown fat may influence the body differently depending on where it is found.

"For example, the axillary, or armpit, area was linked to a decreased risk of high blood pressure compared to other regions," he says. "But overall, patients with brown fat have better glycemic parameters, lipid profiles, and echocardiographic indices, as well as lower inflammatory markers."

These findings indicate that people with brown fat tend to have healthier blood sugar levels, blood fat profiles, measures of heart function, and indicators of inflammation.

Common Blood Pressure Drug Activates Brown Fat

As the researchers investigated medications associated with brown fat activity, they noticed an intriguing pattern. Patients taking angiotensin receptor blockers were more likely to have detectable brown fat on their scans, suggesting that these widely prescribed medications might influence the tissue.

To explore that possibility, the team conducted laboratory experiments using cultured brown fat cells. They found that losartan directly increased the cells' metabolic activity, providing evidence that the drug could stimulate brown fat rather than simply being associated with its presence.

Even more interestingly, the researchers discovered that losartan activated brown fat through molecular pathways different from those responsible for lowering blood pressure. That distinction could be especially valuable for developing future medications that target metabolism without interfering with normal blood pressure regulation.

"The fact that its different effects are mediated by different molecular pathways is advantageous, since it means we could potentially isolate them in future therapies," says Gómez-Banoy. "That way you would be able to stimulate brown fat in people with normal blood pressure."

Additional experiments in healthy mice strengthened the findings. Animals given losartan showed increased energy expenditure, consumed more oxygen, and produced more carbon dioxide, all signs of heightened metabolic activity. Despite these changes, their body weight remained stable.

Brown Fat's Surprising Connection to Mental Health

Beyond its metabolic effects, brown fat may have a previously unrecognized relationship with psychological well-being. The patient analysis revealed that individuals with detectable brown fat had lower rates of anxiety and depression, extending the tissue's potential health associations beyond the cardiovascular system.

"We know that metabolically healthy people tend to have lower incidence of psychiatric diseases, so it could be that having brown fat makes you more metabolically healthy, and this correlates with fewer psychiatric issues," says Gómez-Banoy.

The researchers also found an intriguing relationship involving selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, or SSRIs, medications commonly prescribed to treat depression. These drugs appeared to suppress brown fat activity, suggesting another possible connection between psychiatric treatments and metabolic regulation.

However, the findings do not suggest that brown fat is beneficial in every respect. The analysis also identified higher rates of osteoporosis and certain skin diseases among people with brown fat, raising questions about possible trade-offs that require further investigation.

The discoveries have opened several avenues for future research. Scientists hope to examine the genetics of people with particularly high brown fat activity, investigate why the tissue is associated with lower rates of anxiety and depression, and determine whether its apparent benefits can be harnessed safely.

Losartan may also be only one of several existing medications worth investigating. The extensive patient analysis identified additional drugs associated with brown fat activity, offering researchers a range of potential candidates for future studies.

"There were plenty of other medications associated with brown fat activity in our large cohort," Cohen notes. "This is just a start."

Materials provided by Rockefeller University. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

#4245. Narrowed Focus: 1997 Toyota Camry LE Tested

One of America’s favorite family haulers gets a full makeover.

Over 3,000,000 sold! Call it the McCamry. Along with the Ford Taurus and the Honda Accord, this Toyota is right at the top of the list when Amer­ican families go new-car shopping, and right at the top of the ratings in our last family-sedan comparison test (November 1995). Since its introduction here in 1983, Toyota has diligently smoothed up, slicked up, and suaved up the Camry till the only remaining awkwardness is the unlikely spelling of its name.

That won’t change as Toyota introduces its fourth-­generation Camry in Sep­tember, and neither will the mix of virtues that make this model a favorite. We’re talking refinement of the Camry theme, not reinvention. In fact, the basic platform and powertrain carry on, though engineering improvements seem to touch every part of the car. It’s slightly bigger in each exterior dimension—0.7 inch longer, 0.4 inch wider, 2.1 inches longer in wheelbase; the same four­-cylinder and V-6 engines are modestly more powerful (up 8 hp in the four, up 6 hp in the V-6); and the interior has been upgraded to meet all the safety standards scheduled in the next few years, including the 1997 side-impact and 1999 head-­impact requirements. The aerodynamic drag coefficient has been improved to 0.30, from 0.33.

See all results for used 1997 Toyota Camry for sale near 98029

Toyota is, however, tightening the Camry’s focus. It’s available only as a four-door now in three trim levels: CE, LE, and XLE. Gone is the coupe, which won over just five percent of Camry buyers. Gone, too, is the station wagon, a shape that convinced only three per­cent of Camry buyers in its losing battle against the tide of minivans. (Production of a Camry-based minivan begins next spring.)

In the past, we’ve joked that the Camry’s personality is one of aggressive bland­ness. Unlike the frisky feeling of the Accord and the athletic tautness of the Dodge Intrepid, both of which come through loud and clear before you’ve driven to the first corner, the Camry’s subtlety grows on you over time. It’s smoother, softer, quieter than the others, less com­municative, less mechanical. Instead of talking to you in the very pleasant way of those others, it’s the silent type that, you soon notice, goes expertly about its job.

In this new Camry, Toyota sharpened the expertise without changing the per­sonality. It’s still a car that’s light to the touch: easy to steer, easy to brake. The ride is commendably free of harshness, thanks in part to mounting the suspension on isolated crossmembers front and rear. The four­-cylinder version, with its 195/70SR-14 tires, rides very smoothly and ignores almost completely the road textures that create so much droning in sporting cars. The V-6s come with 205/65HR-15s on six­-inch-wide wheels. These tires are noticeably harsher and noisier than those on the four-cylinder cars, though road nose is still quite reasonable when compared with other cars in this class. Road grip and handling predictability are well above the minimums we’d set for family cars.

See all results for used 1997 Toyota Camry for sale near 98029

The Camry V-6 has been one of the top performers in this class. The 1997 model gains six horsepower (now 194 hp at the same 5200 rpm as the previous peak), gets shorter final-drive gearing (3.93 versus 3.43), and weighs about the same as last year’s smaller car. Another performance plus: A manual transmission has returned to the V-6 lineup, available only on CE models. How­ever, our LE V-6 auto­matic was no quicker than the last LE V-6 we tested, managing 0 to 60 mph in 8.3 seconds. Expect the five-speed to trim that by about four-tenths.

On the road, the automatic’s eagerness to change down a gear or two when you press the pedal, even slightly, and the seamless smoothness of those changes give this car quick reflexes in traffic. The engine revs with the hushed moan of a Lexus. This year, traction control is optional on LE and XLE V-6 models. When it comes to powertrain pleasures, the Camry is world-class.

Still, it’s the more subtle details of pas­senger accommodation that make this Toyota a family favorite. In the previous­-generation Camry, our comparison tests show two adults fit in the back seat more comfortably than in some other brands up to 10 inches longer. We expect this Camry advantage to widen fractionally in this new model because both legroom and head­room in back are increased by a half-inch. Although the Camry is wider on the out­side, energy-absorbing padding to protect in side impacts takes up the extra space and, in certain spots, a little more. The Camry still has pockets in the front doors, unlike the Taurus, which sacrificed them for crash-protection equipment.

Those who wish to maximize rear-seat space should think twice about opting for power front seats (standard equipment on the top-of-the-line XLE). The manual­adjust buckets have excellent toeroom under them, which the power adjuster interrupts with a transverse bar. Tall folks won’t like that.

As in most modern sedans, the Camry has fold-forward rear seatbacks split one­-third and two-thirds, allowing the cargo compartment to be extended into the pas­senger area. Here’s another think-twice: Camrys equipped with the optional child seat—it’s built into the two-thirds section of the rear seat—have that section fixed in place, ruling out all but a narrow passage into the trunk.

At the rear, the trunklid opens wider and lower than before. Space inside, however, is a bit less in the new body—14.1 cubic feet versus 14.8 before. And the new car still has the conventional trunk hinges with the sickle arms that swing down into your luggage when the lid is closed.

Conventional is the right description for the new instrument panel, certainly more conventional than the old one, which tried to visually compartmentalize the cockpit by emphasizing a huge black field in front of the driver. That was the good part. The bad part was the deemphasized and totally boring padding it left for the passenger’s amusement. Now the all-new panel stretches its padding across the inte­rior in an equal-opportunity gesture that makes the interior seem brighter and wider. The glove box is 29 percent larger. The audio controls were raised to a mid­dash height, making them easy to see and reach. The climate controls have changed over to the increasingly common turn-to-adjust knobs. They’re large enough, and so obvious in their workings, that they are easy to operate in their less prominent location. The Camry continues to position its ignition switch in the dash where you can readily see it, instead of hiding it on the side of the steering column.

Toyota has proven itself to be the master of those little conveniences that add up to an exceptionally pleasing car. In this new Camry we see more clever trade-offs as the engineers cut costs, reduce weight, and usually end up serving the customer better, too. For example, the new front bumper cuts the part count nearly in half and saves weight, yet it increases protec­tion to 5 mph from 2.5. Inside, the seats recline in stepless increments now, and the buckets’ height adjusters use a single knob instead of two. Both of these changes cut costs, Toyota says. We say they make the car better, too. Models that previously would have had retracting antennas now have the antenna screened on the rear glass, saving weight and cost. The new Bosch anti-lock brake system weighs half as much as the old one.

Still, not every cost saver is a benefit. The LCD odometer is simply gray num­bers on a gray field, making it less visible than the glowing digits in competitors like the Chrysler Cirrus and the Dodge Stratus. And the new one-piece front-bumper cover now incorporates the grille into its overtly ordinary Rubbermaid-looking façade.

There’s been much speculation in the automotive-trade press about a possible price cut. Don’t hold your breath. Sales of the old Camry hit records earlier this year with no apparent price cutting. Were there sweeteners for the dealer? Sure, but other brands had them, too. Toyota knows all the tricks for selling cars without collapsing its price structure-tricks, we think, that mostly won’t be needed to move this shrewdly updated Camry.

#4244. Genshin Impact Version Luna 4 introduces three new playable characters, including the long-awaited Moon Maiden Columbina

The first major Genshin Impact update in 2026 is almost here, bringing characters we've been waiting a while to play, and more besides.

Genshin Impact’s latest Special Program has spilled all the beans on the game’s next major update, Luna 4. The update, which arrives on January 14, kicks off 2026 with several bits of new content, including some previously-teased characters.

Dubbed Traveler on a Winter's Night, Luna 4 introduces three new playable characters, and brings back The Lantern Rite event to celebrate the beginning of the new year.

The first new arrival in Version Luna 4 is Columbina Hyposelenia, the Moon Maiden. Columbina is a 5-Star Hydro Catalyst wielder. Her kit revolves around supporting the squad via Lunar Reactions. She can trigger coordinated Lunar Reaction DMG, even when she’s off the field.

The Moon Maiden’s special ability, Lunar Domain, further boosts all Lunar Reactions by applying a DMG bonus, including summoning more thundercloud strikes for Lunar-Charged reactions. Columbina is also capable of converting Electro-Charged, Bloom, and Hydro Crystallize reactions into Lunar Reactions, as well as revive fallen squad members.

Speaking of elemental reactions, new in this version is Lunar-Crystallize, a new reaction that’s triggered when Geo meets Hydro (under certain conditions). When triggered, Lunar-Crystallize summons three Moondrifts near enemies. When triggered three times, Moondrift Harmony gets activated, dealing Geo DMG to enemies caught in its radius.

Then there’s Zibai, an Adeptus from Liyue. Zibai is another 5-Star character, a Geo Sword wielder. Zibai can, through entering a special state where they can build up energy, unleash an Elemental Skill that deals Lunar-Crystallize DMG.

The longer the fight goes on, the more Lunar-Crystallize reactions are triggered, the higher (and more often) the damage of Zibai’s Elemental Skill becomes.

Luna 4 continues the Nod-Krai story arc, with a big confrontation with Il Dottore. This is the focus of the new Archon Quest, completing which will earn you a new outfit. There’s a gameplay element to that new chapter, too, with the reveal of Piramida, a new area north of the region. Piramida is the headquarters of the Lightkeepers.

The first phase of Luna 4’s Event Wishes will, unsurprisingly, feature Columbina. It’ll also include reruns of Ineffa. The second phase is when Zibai becomes available, alongside another newcomer: Illuga, a 4-Star, polearm-wielding Geo Lightkeeper. The second phase’s rerun will be Neuvillette, who’s also going to have a new outfit in the shop at a discount.

Version Luna 4 brings back the annual Lantern Rite event, taking place in the mainland of Liyue. The event features its own set of minigames with unique rewards, alongside new stories of the Adepti.

All around Liyue Harbor, you’ll be able to place Xiao Lanterns and inscribe them with messages for others to read. You’ll also earn some Fortune Coins from Auspicious Treasure Trees, which you can later exchange for gifts.

All players will receive 1,600 Primogems through the in-game mail. If you log in regularly, you can earn up to ten Intertwined Fates. Lantern Rite has a new outfit for Yaoyao, which is also where you have a chance to earn one 4-Star Liyue character for free.

Finally, you can look forward to the new Classic Mode in Miliastra Wonderland, which lets you invite select Teyvat characters to join you.

#4242. For better mental health, how often you exercise may matter more than how hard

How often you exercise may matter more for your mental health than how hard you push yourself during a workout. A large study of Norwegian college students found that those who exercised less frequently were more likely to experience depression and anxiety one year later. The findings suggest that maintaining a consistent exercise routine could be particularly important for supporting mental well-being.

The research, published in the open access journal PLOS One, was conducted by Michael Grasdalsmoen of Western Norway University of Applied Sciences and his colleagues. Their results point to the potential benefits of exercising regularly rather than focusing primarily on longer or more demanding workouts.

Why Exercise Habits Matter for Mental Health

Depression, anxiety, and other common mental health conditions are among the leading causes of disability in young adults worldwide. The college years can be an especially challenging period as students adjust to new academic, social, and personal responsibilities. Identifying everyday behaviors that may help protect mental health is therefore an important research priority.

Although previous research has linked regular physical activity to better psychological well-being, many young adults remain physically inactive. Scientists have also had relatively limited evidence about how exercise habits relate to the development of mental health conditions over time, particularly when those conditions are evaluated using standardized diagnostic tools.

To investigate this relationship, Grasdalsmoen and his team followed 10,460 full-time students enrolled in higher education in Norway. Participants ranged in age from 18 to 35.

At the beginning of the study, students completed questionnaires describing their exercise habits, including how frequently they worked out, how strenuous their activities were, how long they exercised, and how many total hours they were active each week. One year later, they completed a self-administered diagnostic assessment designed to identify common mental health disorders.

Exercise Frequency May Matter More Than Intensity

The researchers found that students who reported lower levels of physical activity were more likely to meet diagnostic criteria for anxiety or depression one year later. However, not every aspect of exercise showed the same relationship with mental health.

Exercise frequency emerged as a particularly consistent factor. How often students exercised was more reliably associated with their later mental health than the intensity of their workouts or the amount of time they spent exercising.

The researchers also identified differences between men and women. Among women, lower exercise intensity was associated with a greater likelihood of anxiety and depression. Among men, spending fewer total hours exercising each week showed a stronger association with these conditions.

Overall, the likelihood of common mental health disorders decreased as weekly exercise increased, with this pattern continuing up to approximately 10 hours of physical activity per week.

The results also support the World Health Organization's recommendation that adults complete at least 150 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity each week.

Regular Exercise Could Help Support Student Mental Health

Taken together, the findings suggest that exercising consistently may be especially valuable for reducing the likelihood of anxiety and depression among college students. Rather than concentrating exclusively on workout intensity or duration, maintaining a regular routine could be an important part of supporting mental health.

However, the researchers emphasize that their observational study cannot establish a direct cause-and-effect relationship. Although students who exercised more regularly tended to have better mental health outcomes, the results do not prove that exercise itself prevented depression or anxiety.

Even with this limitation, promoting accessible opportunities for physical activity could be a useful part of broader efforts to improve student well-being. Such efforts may be especially relevant for students who are beginning to experience mental health difficulties or symptoms that have not yet reached the threshold for a clinical diagnosis.

The authors add: "Our findings show that students who engage in regular physical exercise are at lower risk of developing common mental disorders over time. These findings highlight the importance of making physical activity an accessible and natural part of student life."

"Mental health among students is a growing public health concern. Our findings suggest that supporting students to be physically active may contribute to better mental health and should be recognized as an important part of a healthy learning environment."

Funding: The SHoT study was financially supported by the Norwegian Ministry of Education and Research (2017) and the Norwegian Ministry of Health and Care Services (2016). Neither funding organization participated in designing the research, collecting or analyzing data, deciding whether to publish the findings, or preparing the manuscript.

#4241. NIO targets 10,000 battery swap stations and $52B in batteries by 2030

NIO says its energy arm, NIO Power, will operate more than 10,000 battery swap stations and manage over RMB 350 billion ($52 billion) worth of battery packs by 2030.

That’s more than double the swap network NIO runs in China today. And it comes from a company that already missed its last big swap station target.

NIO shared the targets today at NIO IN 2026, its annual technology event, held in Guangzhou to mark the company’s 12th anniversary. NIO Power also expects to deliver over 10 billion kWh of energy per year through charging and battery swapping by the end of the decade.

As of November 11, NIO had 4,252 battery swap stations in China, alongside 5,584 charging stations, according to the company’s latest network count.

Getting to 10,000 by 2030 means adding roughly 1,400 swap stations per year for four straight years. NIO added 679 in 2024 and 681 in 2025. So the new plan needs about double the company’s recent pace.

Even this year’s goal of “at least 1,000” new stations looks tight. NIO had 3,729 swap stations in February when it celebrated its 100 millionth swap, which means it has added just over 500 since then.

There’s also some history here. At its 2021 Power Day, NIO committed to more than 4,000 battery swap stations worldwide by the end of 2025, with about 1,000 of them outside China. By February 2026, it had about 3,700, almost all of them in China.

The energy target is just as aggressive. NIO’s swap network had delivered 5.28 billion kWh in total by February, after roughly eight years of operation. The 2030 goal is nearly twice that every year, although it also counts NIO’s charging stations.

NIO’s swap network is tied to its Battery-as-a-Service (BaaS) model, where customers can buy the car without the pack and rent the battery instead. That means someone has to own a massive fleet of packs, both in customers’ cars and sitting charged in stations. NIO says it wants to manage more than $52 billion of them in four years.

For context, NIO reported total revenue of about $4.7 billion in Q2 2026.

NIO has been moving the heavy capital off its own books. Under deals like its agreement with Zhongan Energy to build 500 swap stations within a year, partners own the stations while NIO handles the technology and operations. NIO Power says it has now co-built more than 900 swap stations with partners.

The hardware is also getting better. NIO opened its first fifth-generation swap stations in August, and they’re the first to serve all three of its brands. That includes the compact firefly, which couldn’t use older stations because of its shorter wheelbase.

NIO CFO Stanley Qu, who also heads NIO Power, presented the unit as NIO’s showcase for running a business with AI agents, using them to manage battery value, station operations, and energy efficiency.

The swap targets were only part of the event; everything else focused on NIO’s AI-fication.

NIO also launched NIO WorldModel (NWM) 3.0, the latest version of its driver-assist AI, which starts rolling out in December to vehicles with the Banyan, Cedar, Cedar S, and Coconut+ systems, pending regulatory clearance.

NIO says NWM 3.0 needs 40% fewer driver interventions than the previous version. It didn’t say how many interventions it started from, which makes the number hard to evaluate. It also claims a roughly 60% boost in drivers’ “sense of reassurance,” whatever that means.

The more concrete claims are about speed: NIO says overall vehicle control latency is down 54% and chassis control latency is down 78%, while training is five times more efficient.

NIO also unveiled NOMI Intelligence 4.0, a rebuild of its in-car assistant around an AI agent framework that can plan and carry out tasks on its own instead of following set commands. The first release, Cedar 2.0.0, will be filed in early December. Cars on Cedar S and Banyan should get it in Q2 2027, followed later by ONVO models.

Finally, CEO William Li pitched NIO as an “AI-native organization.” He argued the global auto industry is worth $7 to $9 trillion and that AI could add more than $1.2 trillion in value to it. NIO says it has deployed over 7,500 AI agents internally, with more than 2.9 million executions so far.

NIO’s swap network is real, and it works. The company passed 130 million swaps this month, and nobody else has built anything close at this scale. Tesla sort of tried battery swapping and quietly dropped it. NIO kept going.

But 10,000 stations by 2030 requires a build pace NIO has never hit, and its last swap target slipped badly. So we’d treat that number as an ambition, not a forecast.

The $52 billion battery figure is the interesting part. It shows what NIO Power really is: a battery asset manager that also builds stations. That only works if partners keep putting up the capital and the batteries keep earning money over their lifetime. NIO has been trying to get other automakers on board for years, with limited results – though it appears to be starting to attract more players.

And the competition isn’t standing still. Chinese automakers like BYD are pushing megawatt-level charging that adds hundreds of kilometers of range in about the time it takes to swap a battery. If ultra-fast charging becomes common, NIO’s swap advantage gets a lot thinner.

Battery swapping is one way to recharge in minutes, but if you drive an EV, charging at home on solar power is still the cheapest way to fuel it. With electricity rates up almost 10% last year and expected to keep climbing, going solar is one of the best ways to protect yourself against rising costs. Heartopia is officially the first big mobile launch of 2026, as the game grabs the attention of millions worldwide.

Heartopia, the new cosy life sim from XD Games, has officially arrived on mobile, right on schedule. If you’ve been keeping up with Heartopia news, you’re likely already aware that the game has pushed back its Steam release to an indeterminate point in 2026.

Doesn’t look like it mattered much, however, as this has already been a big launch on iOS and Android — it probably helps that PC players aren't being entirely left out of the fun, since the game is already available there via XD's own cross-device platform TapTap.

XD Games announced today that Heartopia has reached the top spot on the App Store’s downloads page for free games, and it managed to do so in more than 50 countries and regions worldwide.

The developer is celebratig by offering players a lot of free stuff. If you're feeling lucky, you’ll find new outfits and furniture in three gacha banners (Gilded Acorn Exhibitions): Polar Hymn, The Frostguard, and Coolplayism.

XD Games says you can expect regular updates to add more content, through Fashionwaves and Festivals. In fact, the first season - Winter Frost - is already penciled in for sometime in late January, and it’s going to add appropriately wintery activities like ice skating and snowman-building.

In February, a My Little Pony collaboration event will kick off, bringing new inspired outfits, and vehicles to the game.

Heartopia is a clever mix of Animal Crossing, and The Sims. It’s a free-to-play life sim where you can create your own character, dress them up, build a home for them (and decorate it), and go about town visiting and playing with other players’ characters.

The game’s main feature is the ability to take on a hobby, and seven of those are available at launch. You can dig deep into each hobby, either alone or with others, and there’s a progression track dedicated to each one.

Whether you’re among the millions who downloaded the game already, or you intend to so soon, we’ve got a set of helpful guides to get you started. #4239. Keto diet slashes liver fat by 67% in just 4 months

A ketogenic diet may offer significant health benefits beyond weight loss, according to a new clinical trial that compared three popular approaches to eating. Researchers found that people following a very low-carbohydrate, high-fat diet experienced substantially greater reductions in liver fat than those eating Mediterranean or low-fat diets, even though all three groups lost similar amounts of weight.

The results were especially striking for people with prediabetes. After just four to five months on a ketogenic (or "Keto") diet, approximately half of the participants no longer met the diagnostic criteria for the condition. The findings, published in the journal Cell Metabolism, suggest that the types of foods people eat can influence metabolic health in ways that extend beyond the number of pounds they lose.

"We know weight loss can improve metabolic health in people who are obese," says Samuel Klein, the study's corresponding author at Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis, Missouri. "Our data suggest that if you have high liver fat content and prediabetes, reducing carbohydrate intake can have important therapeutic effects on metabolism beyond just weight loss alone."

Comparing Keto, Mediterranean, and Low-Fat Diets

An estimated 40% of American adults have obesity, a condition associated with increased risks of type 2 diabetes, fatty liver disease, and other health problems. Doctors frequently recommend dietary changes to help patients lose weight and improve their metabolic health, which refers to how effectively the body manages energy, blood sugar, and fats.

Three commonly recommended approaches are low-carbohydrate diets, low-fat diets, and Mediterranean diets. Although each can support weight loss, researchers have been uncertain whether one offers additional metabolic advantages when the amount of weight lost is roughly the same.

These eating patterns differ substantially in their nutritional makeup. Low-carbohydrate approaches, including Atkins and ketogenic diets, restrict carbohydrate consumption, while low-fat diets may obtain as much as 70% of their calories from carbohydrates. The Mediterranean diet emphasizes plant foods such as vegetables, nuts, and olive oil, along with moderate amounts of fish and dairy. Ketogenic diets, meanwhile, can include considerable amounts of fat from animal products, including saturated fat.

To compare their effects, Klein and his colleagues recruited 42 adults with obesity, prediabetes, and fatty liver disease. Prediabetes occurs when blood sugar levels rise above the normal range but have not yet reached the threshold for type 2 diabetes. Fatty liver disease involves excess fat accumulating inside liver cells, which can interfere with the body's ability to regulate metabolism.

A Controlled Clinical Trial With Similar Weight Loss

Participants were randomly assigned to follow one of three diets: ketogenic, Mediterranean, or a low-fat diet emphasizing plant-based foods. To ensure that participants followed their assigned eating plans, the research team supplied all their meals and arranged weekly consultations with a dietitian.

The diets had sharply different proportions of carbohydrates and fat. In the ketogenic group, carbohydrates accounted for just 4% of daily calories, while fat supplied 73%. The Mediterranean group received 50% of its calories from carbohydrates and 35% from fat. The plant-forward group consumed 70% of its calories from carbohydrates and 15% from fat.

Researchers adjusted calorie intake individually so that participants across all three groups lost approximately 10% of their starting body weight. Reaching this target took about four to five months.

By the end of the intervention, every group had experienced meaningful reductions in body fat and improvements in insulin sensitivity. Insulin is the hormone that helps move sugar from the bloodstream into cells, where it can be used for energy. Greater insulin sensitivity makes it easier for the body to maintain healthy blood sugar levels.

However, the similarities between the groups largely ended there.

The ketogenic diet produced the largest improvements in several important indicators of liver function and metabolic health.

Participants following keto experienced an average 67% reduction in liver fat, compared with a 45% reduction in both the Mediterranean and low-fat groups. Because the groups lost comparable amounts of weight, the difference suggests that carbohydrate restriction may influence liver fat through mechanisms beyond weight loss alone.

To investigate these effects, the researchers collected blood samples repeatedly over a 24-hour period, allowing them to observe changes in hormones involved in energy metabolism.

The ketogenic group showed the greatest increase in glucagon, a hormone that helps regulate the body's energy supply and promotes the reduction of fat stored in the liver. Participants on keto also experienced the largest decrease in insulin levels, another change that can help reduce liver fat accumulation.

One result was particularly unexpected. Despite getting nearly three-quarters of their calories from fat, the keto participants did not show an increase in blood fat or cholesterol levels during the study.

"The most surprising finding was that participants in the ketogenic diet group didn't experience an increase in blood fat or cholesterol levels despite consuming the most fat," says Max Petersen, the study's first author at Washington University School of Medicine.

Half of Keto Participants No Longer Had Prediabetes

The benefits extended beyond liver fat. After the weight-loss intervention, approximately 50% of participants assigned to the ketogenic diet no longer met the criteria for prediabetes. By comparison, that milestone was reached by 29% of those on the Mediterranean diet and just 7% of those following the low-fat, plant-forward diet.

These differences are notable because prediabetes signals an elevated risk of developing type 2 diabetes. Bringing blood sugar levels below the prediabetes threshold is an important improvement, although it does not necessarily mean the condition has been permanently reversed.

The findings also highlight a potentially important distinction in weight management: losing weight and improving metabolic health are closely connected, but they are not necessarily the same thing. The composition of a diet may affect how the body handles blood sugar, stores fat, and responds to hormones, even when weight loss is similar.

Researchers emphasize the growing importance of understanding these effects as powerful new obesity treatments become more widely available. GLP-1 medications, which act on hormone pathways involved in appetite and blood sugar regulation, have transformed the treatment of obesity by helping many patients achieve substantial weight loss.

"GLP-1-based medications have revolutionized the therapy of obesity. We now have a very effective pharmacotherapy for achieving significant weight loss," Petersen says. "But in addition, our study shows that the specific composition of the diet can give you added benefits."

Although the trial was relatively small and lasted only four to five months, its carefully controlled design offers evidence that dietary composition can play an important role in metabolic health. Longer studies involving more participants will be needed to determine whether the benefits persist and how different diets compare over time.

The research was supported by the National Institutes of Health and the Foundation for Barnes-Jewish Hospital.

#4238. Volkswagen’s new affordable electric SUV gets a sporty upgrade with GTI DNA

Volkswagen gave its entry-level electric SUV a sporty makeover with GTI-inspired performance. The new ID. Cross R-Line tops the range with added power and style, but there’s more to it than meets the eye.

The new Volkswagen ID. Cross R-Line is now available to order in Germany, starting at €37,225 (about $41,000), including VAT.

While VW’s R-Line is typically just a style and equipment upgrade rather than a true performance upgrade, the range-topping ID. Cross version borrows its electric motor, battery, and chassis from the ID. Polo GTI.

The flagship ID. Cross R-Line model, which will go on sale in March 2027, will use the same 222 hp (166 kW) front-mounted electric motor with up to 290 Nm of torque, which VW said enables it to sprint from 0 to 62 mph (0 to 100 km/h) in 6.9 seconds.

It will also use the same 52 kWh nickel-manganese-cobalt (NMC) battery, providing a WLTP range of up to 266 miles (428 km).

The range-topping version comes with VW’s custom chassis technology, also used in the ID. Polo GTI, which includes an electronically controlled front differential lock, DCC adaptive chassis control, and progressive steering.

As such, the flagship R-Line model is 15 mm lower than the standard ID. Cross. The lower ride height and front differential lock help to improve traction, driving stability, and control, while DCC automatically adjusts to road conditions.

The 222 hp (166 kW) version debuts with an exclusive new Traction profile with different drive modes, including Eco, Comfort, Sport, and Individual.

While pre-sales for the flagship version will open in March 2027, the entry-level ID. Cross R-Line is now available to order in Germany starting at €37,225 (about $41,000), including VAT.

The entry-level version uses a 132 hp (99 kW) electric motor and a 37 kWh battery, providing a WLTP range of up to 195 miles (314 km).

The entry-level version gains “extensive” R-Line standard equipment, including R-Line style bumpers, vertical daytime headlights, and 19″ alloy wheels.

Other standard features include Volkswagen’s interactive ID. Light with LED matrix headlights, Keyless Access, Adaptive Cruise Control (ACC), and a rear-view camera.

Inside, all ID. Cross R-Line models feature sports comfort seats, R-Line trim, and progressive steering as standard. It also gains the Innovision Pro infotainment package with the “IDA” voice assistant.

Volkswagen has yet to reveal prices for the flagship ID. Cross R-Line with the 222 hp (166 kW) and 52 kWh battery, but it will likely be closer to €40,000 ($44,000) when it goes on sale next March. Volkswagen’s ID. Polo GTI electric hot hatch starts at €39,995.

The new R-Line trim comes after Volkswagen opened orders for the standard entry-level ID. Cross last month, starting at €27,995 ($31,000).

What do you think of the new VW ID. Cross R-Line? Would you buy one in the US? Sadly, VW has no plans to bring the entry-level electric SUV to the US, but it will launch the ID. Tiguan in 2027, which will replace the ID.4 SUV.

#4236. EU pushes back Tesla ‘Full Self-Driving’ vote meeting again, now set for December 15

The EU committee that could approve Tesla’s “Full Self-Driving,” now sold in Europe as Tesla Assisted Driving, across the whole bloc won’t meet on December 1 as planned. The meeting is now December 15.

A European Commission spokesperson confirmed the new date to Reuters. The Technical Committee on Motor Vehicles (TCMV) has already discussed Tesla’s file at two meetings without putting it to a vote.

Two weeks isn’t much on its own. But it’s the latest in a long line of European dates that didn’t hold.

In late 2025, Tesla told owners the Dutch regulator RDW had “committed” to approving FSD in February 2026. The RDW publicly corrected it. The Dutch approval came on April 10. Tesla then pointed owners to an EU-wide vote on October 6, and the TCMV agenda for that meeting had no vote on it.

Even the new date took a minute to settle. Belgium’s Flanders transport ministry first said the meeting had moved to December 7 before the Commission clarified it’s December 15. Nobody has given a reason for the change.

And a meeting isn’t a vote. The committee can discuss the file again and push the decision into 2027. Elon Musk said on Tesla’s Q3 call in October that he’d be surprised if EU-wide approval took longer than the first quarter of 2027.

EU-wide approval needs at least 15 of the 27 member states, representing at least 65% of the EU’s population.

Twelve countries have recognized the Dutch approval so far: the Netherlands, Belgium, Croatia, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Latvia, Lithuania, Slovakia, Slovenia, and, last week, Italy, where Tesla has started the rollout. Using Eurostat population figures, we count those 12 at roughly 29% of the EU’s population.

Germany is the obvious next yes. Berlin got Tesla to drop the “Full Self-Driving” name in Europe and then cut the system’s speed margin from 50% to 10% over the limit in exchange for its support. That would bring the yes camp to about 47%.

So Tesla still needs France, or both Spain and Poland, to get over 65%. Not a sure thing. Sweden asked the EU in June to reject the system unless Tesla removed the ability to drive above the posted limit at all.

There’s also a catch for owners. According to Reuters, an EU-level rejection would invalidate the national approvals already granted. If the vote fails, drivers in Italy, the Netherlands, and the 10 other countries who are paying for the system today could lose it.

A two-week slip in a Brussels committee calendar isn’t too bad, but the delays are adding up. It’s December, the committee has other files, and nothing Reuters reported points to a problem specific to Tesla.

Article and headline should consistently refer to it as Tesla Assisted Driving as that is the name which Tesla has agreed to use in the EU. I think the other big question for EU approval is how easily can the driver avoid paying attention to the road.

We also don’t think most owners realize what’s at stake. If this vote goes the wrong way, the national approvals go with it. Italian owners who just got the system would lose it a few weeks later.

What would help Tesla’s case more than a new name and a lower speed cap is data. The RDW still hasn’t published its test results, and Tesla has never released disengagement data in Europe or anywhere else. Governments on the fence, like Sweden, want to see evidence the system is safe, not a rebrand.

December 15 is the next date to watch. Does Tesla walk into that room with Germany, France, or Spain on board, or does this slide into 2027?

#4235. Diablo 4's long-awaited Tower and its Leaderboards enter beta today, and there's no PTR funny business this time

Diablo 4's first big moment of 2026 is nearly upon us, and it's one feature many have been looking forward to for actual years.

Diablo 4 is about to deliver on Blizzard’s years-old promise to add a challenging, leaderboard-driven experience to the action RPG. The beta for The Tower, and its associated Leaderboards are about to kick off.

As recently revealed, the new experience launches today at 11am PT, 2pm ET, 7pm GMT. This is a beta version that arrives alongside update 2.5.2.

This early launch won’t offer the full experience, and it’s mainly designed to get it into the hands of players early so that Blizzard could get as much feedback as possible and incorporate it into the final version.

The beta is available to everyone, which is a nice change from the usual rigmarole players would have to go through to get the PTR build and play on a different branch. The Tower, and Leaderboards will be available only in the Seasonal Realm, however. Indeed, the plan is to build on what’s there with each future season, so it’s best to think of it as a seasonal experience.

The Tower is about as simple of an activity as you can get in an action RPG. The goal is to climb as many floors as you can as quickly as you can, all while battling increasingly difficult mobs.

You need to reach and beat the Tower’s final boss before you can call it a run. The Leaderboard will then show your time, and let you see how well you did compared to other players.

The Tower is available to anyone who completed Rank 2 of the current Season Rank. Once done, an Obelisk will appear in Cerrigar, letting you access the challenge.

The Leaderboards themselves will operate on a two-week schedule, all of which will take place during a given season. In this case, they’re going to close the day before Season of the Divine Interversion - the game’s current season - ends.

Blizzard published an updated set of patch notes that show how much has changed since The Tower, and Leaderboards first became playable in the patch 2.5.0 PTR.

Though the two new additions have been anticipated for a while, there’s not been much exciting going on in the world of Diablo 4, apart, of course, from the surprise arrival of The Paladin class, which became available in December last year to coincide with the announcement of Lord of Hatred, the game’s next expansion.

#4234. 2028 Honda CR-V Is a Fuel-Sipping Hybrid Family SUV Worth Waiting For

Honda’s bestseller goes hybrid only as it enters its seventh generation and will arrive in 2027 with a fresh design inside and out.

Honda’s bestselling model—and the third-bestselling vehicle in the United States through the third quarter of 2026—is getting a complete makeover. The CR-V will follow the path set forth by the sixth-generation Toyota RAV4, going hybrid only as the CR-V enters its seventh generation for the 2028 model year.

We expect the 2028 CR-V Hybrid to wear a sharp new design, with spy photos showing slim daytime running lights above a series of thin horizontal grilles, while the rear end features a light bar that stretches the full width of the SUV. It will likely also be the first vehicle in the U.S. to wear Honda’s new “H” logo, which was originally introduced for its future EVs but will now be applied to other vehicles in its lineup after Honda hurriedly canceled said EVs earlier this year.

The cabin is also expected to get a significant makeover, with the Avancier—a three-row SUV sold in Asia—providing hints about what to expect. The Avancier skips out on most real buttons and knobs, instead putting nearly every function into a large screen mounted to the dashboard, a dramatic shift from Honda’s current setup that prioritizes physical controls. The Avancier’s interior is wrapped in white upholstery, accented by glowing ambient lighting, and features a squared-off steering wheel. Honda also appears to be switching to a column-mounted gear selector.

See all results for new 2028 Honda CR-V Hybrid for sale near 60004

While Honda was once led by the Accord and Civic sedans, in today’s SUV-obsessed market, the CR-V has become the Japanese automaker’s most important model. Its biggest rival, the RAV4, was overhauled for 2026 and went hybrid only. Now, the CR-V will follow suit to stay competitive in the incredibly crowded compact SUV segment. Hybrid sales of the current-generation CR-V have been strong, accounting for over half of the SUV’s total sales so far this year, making it a perfect choice to launch Honda’s new platform and hybrid powertrain.

The CR-V will arrive on a new platform that Honda promises will be stiffer and lighter than before, taking a modular approach that will lead to greater parts sharing and reducing costs. This platform will presumably be adapted to underpin future versions of the Accord and Civic, along with Acura models such as the upcoming next-generation RDX Hybrid.

Honda will ditch the standard 190-hp 1.5-liter four-cylinder engine for the 2028 CR-V, which will arrive exclusively with the company’s new hybrid powertrain. The fifth generation of Honda’s two-motor hybrid setup will continue to use an Atkinson-cycle four-cylinder, along with a pair of electric motors, but the 2.0-liter engine will be a fresh design, featuring a new cooling system. As before, the electric motors will power the wheels most of the time, but the gas engine can also be engaged to directly drive the wheels.

See all results for new 2028 Honda CR-V Hybrid for sale near 60004

The electric motors are more compact than before, and Honda has developed a new battery too. The company says the new hybrid setup will bring improved power and efficiency, targeting 10 percent better fuel economy than the outgoing hybrid powertrain. The current CR-V Hybrid makes 205 horsepower and is rated at up to 38 mpg combined. We wouldn’t be surprised to see power increase to over 220 hp—the RAV4 makes 226 hp in FWD form and 236 hp with AWD—and fuel economy nudge up to just over 40 mpg.

The CR-V is expected to come with front-wheel drive standard and all-wheel drive optional, although it’s unclear if the latter will see the addition of a third electric motor. Honda will also likely include the S+ Shift feature seen on the Civic Hybrid and Prelude, which simulates a traditional transmission’s gearchanges and allows the driver to manually shift with the steering-wheel paddles.

The CR-V’s chief rival will continue to be the Toyota RAV4. However, the Hyundai Tucson Hybrid and Nissan Rogue Hybrid, which both enter a new generation for 2027, will also be strong competitors. The Jeep Cherokee, Kia Sportage Hybrid, and Subaru Forester Hybrid will be in the mix too, along with nonhybrid compact SUVs like the Volkswagen Tiguan.

The move to only offer a hybrid powertrain could see the CR-V’s entry price climb, which might alienate some buyers. Honda will also need to make sure it can match or exceed the efficiency of rivals like the RAV4 while still providing adequate performance and a spacious, usable cabin, given how closely matched the compact SUV space is these days. Moving away from physical interior controls could also upset the Honda faithful who are used to the company’s simple-to-use buttons.

Production is set to kick off at Honda’s factories in East Liberty, Ohio, and Greensburg, Indiana, in April 2027. Sales should begin shortly after, and with the current CR-V Hybrid starting at $37,580, we expect the next-generation model to come in at around $38,000.

#4233. Microplastics may be more dangerous than we thought. Scientists just discovered why

Plastic is used in everything from food packaging and water bottles to children's toys, largely because it is considered chemically stable and unlikely to react with its surroundings. However, new research suggests that this assumption may not hold when plastic breaks down into extremely small particles.

As larger plastic objects fragment into microplastics and even smaller nanoplastics, the amount of exposed surface area increases dramatically. Scientists have now discovered that these newly exposed surfaces can interact with water in unexpected ways, producing reactive molecules that may harm living cells.

Researchers at Columbia University and the University of California, Berkeley identified the chemical processes behind this phenomenon in a new study published in Nature. Their findings challenge the longstanding idea that microplastics are simply passive fragments of material.

"As plastic fragments into smaller and smaller particles, its surface area increases enormously. Then microplastics change the water that surrounds them, generating high-energy, reactive radicals (reactive oxygen species, ROS) that very likely contribute to biological damage that we see in animals and potentially in humans as a result of microplastic exposure," said Wei Min, a Columbia professor of Chemistry and Biomedical Engineering.

Why Microplastics Could Be Dangerous Inside the Human Body

The discovery raises important questions about what happens when microplastics enter the human body. Blood and cells contain large amounts of water, creating conditions in which these tiny particles could continue participating in chemical reactions.

Rather than remaining inactive after exposure, microplastics may generate reactive oxygen species, often called ROS. These highly reactive molecules can damage biological structures, including components of cells and tissues. The findings offer a possible explanation for some of the harmful effects associated with microplastic exposure, although they do not establish that this process causes specific diseases in humans.

The research builds on earlier work by Min's laboratory that helped reveal just how widespread microscopic plastic contamination has become.

In a widely reported 2024 study, the Columbia researchers developed a laser-based microscopy technique capable of detecting extremely small plastic particles. Using this technology, they found an average of approximately 240,000 detectable plastic fragments in a single liter of bottled water (mostly nanometer-sized plastic, nanoplastics). That was 10 to 100 times more particles than previous estimates had suggested.

The discovery helped draw greater attention to the presence of microplastics and nanoplastics throughout the food system.

Growing Concerns About Microplastics and Human Health

Since that earlier research attracted widespread attention, the potential health consequences of microplastic exposure have become an increasingly important public health issue.

In 2026, the federal government launched a $144 million initiative focused on addressing toxic microplastics in the human body. The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency also added microplastics to a federal list of contaminants that may be of concern in drinking water, marking their first appearance on the list.

Meanwhile, studies published in major scientific journals, including the New England Journal of Medicine, Nature Medicine, and Nature Health, have reported associations between exposure to microplastics and nanoplastics and serious conditions such as heart attacks, strokes, dementia, and brain tumors.

However, an important question has remained unanswered. If plastic is generally considered chemically inert, how might these microscopic fragments contribute to biological damage?

The new findings identify a previously overlooked chemical pathway that could help researchers understand these potential health risks.

"Our research found that when microplastics interact with water, as they do when they're in bottled water, or when they're absorbed into our bloodstream, they spontaneously generate what we call reactive oxygen species (ROS)," said Naixin Qian, a postdoctoral researcher in Wei Min's lab who helped lead the research. "ROS are textbook examples of the kinds of molecules that can damage animal and human tissue."

How Water Triggers Harmful Chemical Reactions

One of the most surprising aspects of the discovery is that water plays an active role in the reaction.

Many plastics are hydrophobic, meaning their surfaces repel water. When water encounters these surfaces, the molecules and electrically charged particles near the boundary can behave differently than they do in ordinary water.

The researchers found that these interactions can encourage electrons to move between chemical species, allowing highly reactive radicals to form. As plastic fragments become smaller, their greater surface area provides more locations where these reactions can occur.

"Water is a key active player here, rather than just a spectator. It's integral to making these microplastics reactive. Water molecules become chemically active when they come into contact with plastic, which is hydrophobic. Contact between the water and plastic creates an environment that facilitates electron transfer, and the formation of reactive radicals. When plastics fragment into smaller particles, their increasing surface-to-volume ratio creates more of these chemically active areas," Min said.

To investigate the process, the Columbia researchers performed chemical and biological experiments. Their collaborators in Professor Teresa Head-Gordon's laboratory at UC Berkeley used theoretical calculations and computer simulations to examine the interactions between plastic surfaces and water at the molecular level.

The Berkeley team developed a theoretical explanation showing how hydroxide ions, which are negatively charged particles, can become concentrated in the layers of water immediately surrounding a water-repelling plastic surface. In this environment, the ions can more readily lose electrons and form hydroxyl radicals.

Hydroxyl radicals are particularly reactive chemical species capable of damaging biological molecules. Their formation provides a possible link between the physical breakdown of plastics and the biological effects researchers have observed.

Could the Discovery Lead to Safer Plastics?

Understanding the chemistry involved could eventually help scientists develop plastics that are less likely to generate harmful reactive molecules when exposed to water.

"Our fundamental work that the most hydrophobic microplastics interacting with water can drive chemical reactivity could ultimately lead to new engineering solutions by redesigning the chemistry of these commodity plastics to reduce the toxic outcomes on health and the environment," said Head-Gordon.

The implications also extend beyond human health. Microplastics can enter rivers, lakes, and other waterways through industrial waste, wastewater, and everyday activities. The newly identified chemical reactions could influence aquatic organisms and ecosystems exposed to these particles.

Co-author Beizhan Yan of Columbia University's Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory emphasized that microplastics can originate from numerous sources, including plastic manufacturing facilities and laundromats. Everyday processes, such as heating materials in a microwave or leaving bottled water exposed to sunlight during storage, can also contribute to the formation of tiny plastic particles.

"This work has significant implications for environmental and human health," said co-author Beizhan Yan of Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory. "In certain environments, such as discharges from plastic manufacturers and laundromats, microplastics can form and enter aquatic environments. This work also indicates that radicals can form on hydrophobic plastic surfaces in water, which could affect ecosystems and human health following exposure. In addition, various uses and processes in our daily lives can generate microplastics, including microwave heating, sunlight exposure of bottled water during storage. This foundational work provides a potential pathway for understanding their health impacts."

By revealing that microplastics can actively alter the chemistry of surrounding water, the research adds a new dimension to concerns about plastic pollution. It also establishes a potential mechanism for investigating how these widespread particles interact with living systems, while opening the door to strategies for reducing their environmental and health risks.

Materials provided by Columbia University. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

#4231. The Sims developer vows "our values are unchanged," as it teases multiple projects from post-Saudi-owned EA

The team behind one of EA's most diverse franchises has issued a statement about its future under the soon-to-be Saudi-owned publisher.

In their (slightly belated) new years message to players, the developer of EA’s The Sims series of games has lightly addressed concerns about its future within the publisher in a wide-ranging letter to the community.

The letter also serves as something of a light plan for what players can expect soon, and in the future, alongside what the various teams are currently working on.

The developer starts off the yearly check-in with a statement that attempts to address concerns about the future of The Sims, historically one of EA’s most inclusive and culturally diverse franchises.

This, of course, comes in the wake of last year’s bombshell that EA is being taken private by a coalition led by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF), alongside investment firms Silver Lake Capital and Affinity Partners. The $55 billion acquisition was approved by EA’s shareholders in December, and is set to close by the end of June.

Understandably, many raised concerns about what EA’s new ownership would mean for its people, and portfolio of games. The news is concerning for The Sims in particular, a series that’s long embraced diversity and inclusivity, and has historically been popular among women, people of colour, and members of the LGBTQ+ community.

“Our Sims team's creative control, guided by our values of inclusivity, choice, creativity, community, and play, has not changed,” the post reads, though without referring to the buyout directly at any point.

“These values inspire the decisions we make each and every day as we plan for today, tomorrow, and the future.”

As for what’s to come in 2026 and beyond, it sounds like The Sims team has multiple irons in the fire. The developer is working on “a family of new Sims experiences” that will find homes on PC, console, and mobile. Crucially, the post says that not every experience will be on every platform, in order for each to focus on delivering something different and interesting.

Future releases, of course, include new The Sims 4 content that focuses on the single-player experience. The social and more multiplayer-driven experiences, however, will instead be found in Project Rene, the mobile-first life-sim currently in development. (Despite early confidence that it was a working title for The Sims 5, it's now confirmed that Project Rene won’t, in fact, be a direct successor to The Sims 4.)

Some of these projects will see more playtesting throughout 2026, so you should probably sign up for The Sims Labs if you want to hear about when/how you can get involved.

#4230. The Suzuki Ignis is back, and this time it will be a low-cost EV sold globally [Images]

Suzuki offered a first look at the all-new Ignis, its first compact EV designed specifically for global markets.

The first-generation Ignis went on sale back in 2000 as a three- and five-door hatchback, and in 2016, Suzuki reintroduced it as a compact crossover.

After discontinuing the gas-powered version just last year, Suzuki is now bringing the Ignis back. This time, as a fully electric compact EV.

Suzuki revealed the all-new Ignis EV on Wednesday, deeming it the brand’s “first compact EV for global markets.”

The electric city car is based on the original Ignis and clearly draws inspiration from the e Sky, Suzuki’s first kei EV that debuted last month in Japan.

Unlike the e Sky, the new Ignis EV is designed for global markets, including Europe. Suzuki said the Ignis was developed under the concept of “Easy to Switch,” which, as you can guess, means it’s designed to make it easy for drivers to switch from a gas-powered car to electric.

To ensure it can handle urban areas and winding roads in Europe and other regions, Suzuki put the electric city car through “extensive testing” on public roads.

Suzuki fine-tuned the chassis and power delivery specifically for the different road conditions and needs of drivers in major global markets.

The global Ignis EV is also slightly larger than the e Sky, measuring 3,570 mm long, 1,565 mm wide, and 1,635 mm tall, with a 2,460 mm wheelbase.

It’s built on the same dedicated “HEARTECT-e” EV platform as the e Sky, with a single electric motor that delivers 90 hp (67 kW) and 98 lb-ft (133 Nm) of torque.

The Ignis also uses the same 26 kWh lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery as the e SKY. However, Suzuki hasn’t revealed driving range figures yet. Suzuki didn’t specify, but the LFP battery pack used in the e SKY is supplied by BYD’s battery unit to keep costs down.

According to Suzuki, the e SKY for Japan offers a WLTC driving range of up to 310 km (192 miles) and a “class-leading” AC energy consumption rating of 97 Wh/km.

Inside, the new Suzuki Ignis EV adopts a similar setup to the e Sky with a space-maximizing four-seat layout and a wide infotainment display.

Suzuki will launch the Ignis in Europe and other markets starting in summer 2027. Prices have yet to be announced, but the Ignis will enter an increasingly competitive segment of entry-level compact EVs, including the Renault Twingo, BYD Dolphin Surf, and Honda Super-N.

In Japan, Suzuki’s e SKY undercuts much of the competition with prices starting at just ¥2,120,000 ($13,500).

For context, the Renault Twingo E-Tech starts at under €19,490 ($21,500) in Europe and £14,745 in the UK. BYD’s Dolphin Surf starts at around €22,990 ($25,500) and £18,675 ($24,500) in the UK, while the Honda Super-N starts at £18,995 ($25,000) in the UK.

Which compact EV would you drive? Let us know in the comments. Unfortunately, none of them will be coming to the US.

#4229. Ineos to Build Grenadiers in America and Sell Its French Plant to BYD

The fledgling automaker could start manufacturing its off-road-centric vehicles in the United States as soon as 2028.

The Ineos Grenadier SUV and Quartermaster pickup truck could be trading the French-flag badges that signal their Hambach production for ones that feature America’s stars and stripes. That’s because the fledgling British automaker has now confirmed plans to begin building its vehicles in the United States, with the first American-made Ineos models scheduled for 2028.

Ineos Automotive is still determining the exact location of its planned American production facility, but it says that it has developed a shortlist of potential sites. The move will bring the brand’s production to its largest market, with the United States making up around 70 percent of Ineos’s global sales.

See all results for new 2027 Ineos Grenadier Quartermaster for sale near 29210

Since Ineos already sells most of its vehicles in the U.S., the move will help make the brand more efficient. By building its vehicles in America, Ineos will also be able to avoid paying many of the lofty import tariffs that it’s currently subjected to. Plus, along with announcing plans to move to the United States, Ineos confirmed it’s in the process of selling its current Hambach facility to Chinese automotive giant BYD.

At this point, Ineos hasn’t announced whether it plans to buy an existing manufacturing facility, build a new one, or use another automaker’s excess capacity. One thing Ineos has been clear about, though, is that the move will cover its entire global production. A final decision on the facility is expected within the next few months to keep the move on schedule.

#4228. NASA's powerful Moon rocket engine roars through a dramatic 200-second test

NASA has successfully completed another powerful rocket engine test as the agency prepares for future Artemis missions that will return astronauts to the Moon and lay the groundwork for human exploration of Mars.

On November 18, engineers fired RS-25 engine No. 10001 at the Fred Haise Test Stand at NASA's Stennis Space Center, located near Bay St. Louis, Mississippi. The developmental engine ran for its full scheduled duration of three minutes and 20 seconds (200 seconds).

Although this particular engine is not intended for spaceflight, the successful test will provide NASA and its primary contractor, L3Harris Technologies, with valuable performance data. Engineers will use the results to improve the power, efficiency, and reliability of RS-25 engines designed for upcoming Artemis missions.

Powerful RS-25 Engines Will Help Send Astronauts Back to the Moon

NASA is preparing for Artemis IV, a mission scheduled for 2028 that aims to land astronauts on the lunar surface. The mission will launch from NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida, using the massive Space Launch System (SLS) rocket to carry astronauts aboard the Orion spacecraft.

Artemis IV represents an important step toward NASA's larger ambitions. The agency plans to explore the Moon's South Pole, establish a sustained human presence on the lunar surface, and develop the experience and technologies needed for the first crewed journey to Mars.

The RS-25 engines play a crucial role in making these missions possible. Each SLS rocket uses four of the engines, which together generate up to 2 million pounds of thrust to help propel the spacecraft off the launchpad and into space.

Before any RS-25 engine is cleared for flight, it must undergo testing at NASA's Stennis Space Center to verify that it can perform reliably under the extreme conditions of a rocket launch.

These tests are carried out by specialists from NASA, L3Harris Technologies, and Nova Space Solutions, working together to ensure the engines are ready to power future journeys beyond Earth.

Hyundai’s new IONIQ 3 checks all the boxes as an affordable EV: it offers over 300 miles of range, a practical interior, and Hyundai’s new Pleos infotainment system. So, will Hyundai bring it to the US?

The Hyundai IONIQ 3 is now on sale across Europe and the UK as a smaller sibling to the IONIQ 5, positioned between the Inster EV and Hyundai Kona Electric.

Although it’s part of the IONIQ sub-brand, the IONIQ 3 features a new “Aero Hatch” design. The new look “reimagines the compact EV silhouette,” Hyundai said, designed to optimize efficiency and interior space.

The response so far has been “extraordinary,” Ashley Andrew, president of Hyundai Motor UK, said after launching the IONIQ 3 last month.

According to Andrew, the compact EV received “more customers registering their interest before launch than any new Hyundai we’ve introduced in the UK,” and that’s including gas-powered and electric vehicles.

The first reviews of the IONIQ 3 have been overwhelmingly positive, highlighting its efficiency, practical interior, and affordable price tag.

Update 11/25/2026: A Hyundai spokesperson told Electrek that “it’s likely that the IONIQ 3 that was apparently spotted in the US recently was the same unit that was brought in for World Car of the Year’s annual test days” held in Pasadena, California.

It looks like the IONIQ 3 will be another affordable, practical EV the US will miss out on.

A post shared by KindelAuto (@kindelauto)

The update from Hyundai comes after the IONIQ 3 was recently captured driving on public US roads, raising speculation, or perhaps hope, that it will come to the States after all.

The model spotted in the images from KindelAuto is the IONIQ 3 N Line, a sportier, higher-priced trim.

While it’s among the first sightings in the US, we have seen several Hyundai Motor Group electric vehicles testing in the US that are still not available and likely won’t ever be, such as Kia’s EV5 SUV and PV5 van.

The IONIQ 3 is built at Hyundai Motor’s Izmit, Turkey, plant and is specifically designed for European drivers.

In Europe and the UK, Hyundai offers the IONIQ 3 with two battery packs: 42 kWh and 61 kWh. The base IONIQ 3 Advance trim with the 42 kWh battery starts at £18,495 ($25,000) OTR and offers up to 213 miles of WLTP range. That’s including the UK’s £3,750 Electric Car Grant.

The IONIQ 3 Advance with the 61 kWh battery starts at £21,995 ($29,000) and offers a “class-leading” WLTP range of up to 308 miles. That also includes the UK government ECG grant.

Measuring 4,155 mm (163.5″) long, 1,800 mm (70.9″) wide, and 1,505 mm (59.3″) high, with a wheelbase of 2,680 mm (105.5″), Hyundai’s electric hatch is even smaller than the Kia EV3 and Volkswagen ID.3.

The IONIQ 3 is also Hyundai’s first vehicle in Europe equipped with its new Pleos Connect infotainment system.

Hyundai’s new system is more like using a smartphone. It’s based on the Android Automotive OS with apps and customizable screens, similar to Tesla models. It’s available in the IONIQ 3 with a 12.9″ or 14.6″ center infotainment screen, plus an optional driver display.

Unlike the larger IONIQ 5, the IONIQ 3 uses a 400V architecture. However, the 42 kWh battery can still recharge from 10% to 80% in about 29 minutes. The 61 kWh battery takes around 30 minutes.

In Germany and other European markets, Hyundai’s compact IONIQ 3 starts at about €28,950 ($33,000).

While Hyundai currently has no plans to bring the IONIQ 3 to the US, it does sell the IONIQ 5, built at the Hyundai Motor Group Metaplant America outside Savannah, GA, alongside the three-row IONIQ 9.

Starting at about $35,000, Hyundai’s IONIQ 5 has remained among the top-selling electric vehicles in the US outside of the Tesla Model Y and Model 3.

In fact, Hyundai was just named the “Best Electric Vehicle Brand” by US News & World Report for the first time for 2027.

The currently ongoing Season 1 was initially meant to end on Tuesday, January 20, hence why the developer had to communicate something this week.

Escalating the fight with new threats on the battlefield.Season 2 begins February 17. pic.twitter.com/fGMegJJuTj

What we are getting news of today, however, is the game’s next patch. This extension update is going to arrive next week, on January 20, when Season 1 was supposed to end.
